reference: GNU sed from the runner's read-only /usr tree is the parity oracle; each parity case runs the same script under reference Bash with GNU sed on PATH and under bash-os with PATH empty. Cases that need multibyte behaviour export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 themselves.
coverage: UTF-8 y/// character pairing and \U \L \u \l case conversion of non-ASCII letters (guest pass 3).
a/i/c text to the end of the line in every form (one-liner, a\ plus newline, -e continuation, -f files), and sed -i through search-only directories (guest pass 6).
exclusions: Unibyte-locale y/// and case conversion are covered by suites/sed.json.

cases.purpose: In a UTF-8 locale y/// pairs characters, not bytes (y/éà/ea/ used to fail with 'SET1 and SET2 must be same length'), and \U \L \u \l convert non-ASCII letters (guest pass 3, G49).
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf 'éàx\n' | sed 'y/éà/ea/'
printf 'abc\n' | sed 'y/abc/αβγ/'
printf 'αβγ abc\n' | sed 'y/αβγ/abc/'
printf 'école ÉCOLE ça\n' | sed 's/.*/\U&/'
printf 'École ÉCOLE\n' | sed 's/.*/\L&/'
printf 'école\n' | sed 's/.*/\u&/'
printf 'École\n' | sed 's/\(.\)\(.*\)/\l\1\U\2/'
printf 'x\n' | sed 's/x/\Uéà\E-é/'
printf 'é\n' | sed 'y/é/ab/' 2>/dev/null || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: sed -i needs only search permission on the directories above the file and search plus write permission on its own directory, like a 0711 home directory seen by another user; it used to open every path component for reading and fail with 'Permission denied' (guest pass 6, G102). The [ -r ] lines prove read permission is really withheld.
cases.script:
mkdir -p x/w y/v
echo a > x/w/f
echo a > y/v/f
chmod 0311 x y/v
[ -r x ] || echo x-unreadable
[ -r y/v ] || echo v-unreadable
sed -i s/a/b/ "$PWD/x/w/f"
sed -i s/b/c/ x/w/f
sed -i.bak s/c/d/ x/w/f
sed -i s/a/b/ y/v/f
(cd y/v && sed -i.orig s/b/c/ f)
cat x/w/f x/w/f.bak y/v/f
chmod 0755 x y/v
ls x/w y/v
